---
id: "smk-04"
title: "Emperor penguin"
---

The emperor penguin is the tallest and heaviest of all living penguin species and is found only in Antarctica. Adults stand about 1.1 metres tall and can weigh up to 40 kilograms. The species breeds during the Antarctic winter on the sea ice: after the female lays a single egg she returns to the sea to feed, while the male incubates the egg on his feet under a fold of skin for about two months, huddling with other males against winds and temperatures far below freezing. Emperor penguins feed on fish, krill and squid and are remarkable divers, reaching depths of more than 500 metres and staying under water for over twenty minutes. Their dense feathers and layers of fat insulate them from the cold. Chicks are covered in grey down and are fed by both parents until they fledge in summer. The species is considered near threatened because of the loss of sea ice.
